facts.statement: Cruxicheiros is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived in the Middle Jurassic of England.
facts.quote: Cruxicheiros (meaning "cross hand") is a genus of theropod dinosaur which lived in the Middle Jurassic of England.

facts.statement: The type species C. newmanorum was described by Roger Benson and Jonathan Radley in 2010.
facts.quote: The type species is C. newmanorum, described by Roger Benson and Jonathan Radley in 2010.

facts.statement: The holotype remains were discovered in the early 1960s at Cross Hands Quarry near Little Compton, Warwickshire, England.
facts.quote: The remains of the holotype were discovered in the early 1960s in the Cross Hands Quarry, near Little Compton, in Warwickshire in England.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the lower Bathonian stage of the Middle Jurassic, approximately 167 million years ago.
facts.quote: These fossils came from the Chipping Norton Limestone Formation, which is dated to the lower Bathonian stage of the Middle Jurassic, about 167 mya (million years ago).

facts.statement: In 2010, researchers recognized that the Cross Hands Quarry fossils differed from those previously attributed to Megalosaurus.
facts.quote: The 2010 paper recognized differences between the Cross Hands Quarry discovery and those attributed to Megalosaurus.

facts.statement: Cruxicheiros is distinguished from Megalosaurus by having lower and broader back spines and differences in leg and hip bones.
facts.quote: These differences include lower and broader spines along the animal's back, and differences in leg and hip bones.

facts.statement: The genus name Cruxicheiros combines Latin and Greek words for "cross" and "hand" to reference the Cross Hands Quarry locality.
facts.quote: The generic name Cruxicheiros comes from a mixture of Latin and Greek, Latin crux meaning "cross" and Greek cheir meaning "hand", in reference to the Cross Hands Quarry locality where the fossils were discovered.

facts.statement: The species name newmanorum honors the Newman family, who owned the quarry.
facts.quote: The specific name newmanorum honors the Newman family, who own the quarry.

facts.statement: Cruxicheiros was a large theropod, though the known fossil material is very limited.
facts.quote: Cruxicheiros was a large theropod, but the known material is very limited.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, cataloged as WARMS G15770, consists of a partial right femur.
facts.quote: The holotype, cataloged as WARMS G15770, is a partial right femur.

facts.statement: In 2012, Thomas Holtz estimated the length of Cruxicheiros at 9 meters (29.5 feet).
facts.quote: In 2012 Thomas Holtz estimated its length at 9 meters (29.5 feet).

facts.statement: Cruxicheiros is classified as a tetanuran, a group of dinosaurs that includes theropods like Tyrannosaurus and Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: Cruxicheiros was a tetanuran, a member of the dinosaur group Tetanurae which also includes theropods such as Tyrannosaurus and Spinosaurus.

facts.statement: Due to classification uncertainties, Cruxicheiros is classified as Tetanurae incertae sedis.
facts.quote: In view of the uncertainties they classified Cruxicheiros as Tetanurae incertae sedis.

facts.statement: Cruxicheiros lived in the middle Jurassic period, approximately 167 million years ago during the Bathonian stage, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 167 millones de años durante el Bathoniense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: The generic name Cruxicheiros derives from Latin and Greek words for "cross" and "hands," referencing the Cross Hands Quarry discovery site.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico Cruxicheiros proviene de la mezcla de las palabras en latín crux que significa "cruz" y del griego, cheiros "manos", en referencia de la Cantera de Cross Hands donde los fósiles fueran descubiertos.

facts.statement: Due to uncertainties, researchers classified Cruxicheiros as Tetanurae incertae sedis.
facts.quote: Debido a las dudas clasificaron a Cruxicheiros como Tetanurae incertae sedis.

facts.statement: The time range for Cruxicheiros is the Bathonian stage, from 168.2 to 165.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Bathonian (168.2 to 165.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Cladistic analysis suggested three equally probable positions for Cruxicheiros: as the most basal neotetanuran, the most basal megalosauroid, or the most basal member of Tetanurae.
rejected.quote: They performed a cladistic analysis which rendered three equally probable positions for Cruxicheiros: as the most basal neotetanuran, as the most basal megalosauroid, or as the most basal member of the Tetanurae.
